period_note: Balance-sheet-free, income-statement-only interim snapshot -- Solo/Standalone presumed (see sources.json). Recovered via a Wayback Machine capture of DSE's OWN company page (dsebd.org/displayCompany.php?name=PUBALIBANK), NOT the bank's site -- the technique proven on RUPALIBANK, applied here for the first time to PUBALIBANK. This vintage of the table (titled 'Financial Performance: <year>', pre-2016) gives only Turn Over, Net Profit After Tax (Continuing Operations), Basic/Diluted EPS and NAV per share, ALL CUMULATIVE FROM JAN 1 per the table's own column headers (Q1=3 Months, Q2=6 Months, Q3=9 Months) -- no period-end market price is given in this table vintage (the top-of-page 'Last Trade' price reflects the capture date, not the quarter-end, so it is not usable and not recorded). Sourced from DSE's (dsebd.org) own company-page interim table, NOT the bank's own site (pubalibangla.com, Cloudflare-blocked). Solo/Standalone basis presumed, consistent with this bank's established series basis, but not explicitly labeled solo vs consolidated on the DSE page itself -- flagged as an assumption, not a confirmed fact (same caveat documented for RUPALIBANK's use of this identical source type). Q1's Basic EPS (0.92) implies ~496.86mn weighted-average shares (456.84/0.92), matching the PRE-bonus share count before the 24/04/2011 AGM's 35% bonus issue for FY2010 (670,761,000 total securities / 1.35 = 496,860,000, almost exactly) -- Q2 and Q3 instead reconcile against the NEW 670.761mn post-bonus count (1193.69/1.78=670.7mn; 1713.52/2.55=672.0mn). This is the clearest instance of a pattern (Q1 filed on the pre-AGM share count, Q2/Q3 on the post-AGM count, no retroactive Q1 restatement) that recurs across multiple years in this bank's series whenever a bonus/stock dividend falls between Q1 and Q2 -- see insights.json. Q3 2011's own NAV-per-share cell reads a suspicious flat 0.000 immediately after two real values (22.12, 22.85 in Q1/Q2) -- treated as non-disclosure and excluded per this dataset's 'don't record a suspicious flat zero at face value' rule, not as a genuine NAV collapse to zero.
